    Messaging¶

    See the Messaging guide.

    rn_forge.django.messaging ¶

    Transactional outbox and inbox messaging over the Django ORM.

    Import from the submodules; this app package cannot import models before Django's app registry is ready.

    MessagingConfig ¶

    Bases: AppConfig

    The messaging app. Its models are abstract, so it adds no tables.

    Models¶

    rn_forge.django.messaging.models ¶

    Abstract transactional outbox and inbox models.

    AbstractInboxMessage ¶

    Bases: Model

    A received message, recorded so a redelivery is recognised.

    message_id accepts identifiers assigned by either the sender or broker.

    AbstractOutboxMessage ¶

    Bases: Model

    An event written in the same transaction as the change that caused it.

    Preserve the (published_at, occurred_at) index when overriding Meta.

    Relay¶

    rn_forge.django.messaging.relay ¶

    The outbox relay: claim, publish and mark one batch.

    make_outbox_relay(outbox_model, bus, *, envelope_builder, batch_size=100, on_lag_observed=None, log=None, clock=timezone.now) ¶

    Build a callable that claims, publishes and marks one batch of outbox rows.

    Rows are claimed with select_for_update(skip_locked=True) in transaction.atomic(). A publish error rolls the claim back, so delivery is at least once.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    outbox_model type[M]

    The consuming app's concrete outbox model.

    		 required
    bus MessageBus

    Where messages go.

    		 required
    envelope_builder Callable[[M], Mapping[str, Any]]

    Row → the event mapping published. Called once per row.

    		 required
    batch_size int

    The most rows claimed per call.

    		 100
    on_lag_observed Callable[[float], None] | None

    Called once per non-empty batch with the age, in seconds, of its oldest row — wire it to your metrics backend.

    		 None
    log Log | None

    Receives outbox.relay per non-empty batch. Defaults to AppLogger at info.

    		 None
    clock Callable[[], datetime]

    Supplies published_at and the lag reference.

    		 now

    Consumer¶

    rn_forge.django.messaging.consumer ¶

    The inbox consumer: dedupe, dispatch and record one inbound event.

    UnknownMessageType(message, *message_args, error_code=-1, **error_data) ¶

    Bases: AppException

    No handler is registered for the event's type.

    check(value, message, *message_args, **kwargs) classmethod ¶

    Raise this exception if value is falsy.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    value Any

    The value to test.

    		 required
    message str

    Exception message (supports positional format args).

    		 required
    *message_args Any

    Forwarded to message.format().

    		 ()
    **kwargs Any

    Forwarded as error_code / error_data to the constructor.

    		 {}

    Example::

    AppException.check(path.exists(), "Missing file: {}", path, error_code=404)

    process_event(event, registry, inbox_model, *, id_key='id', type_key='type', clock=timezone.now) ¶

    Handle event once, however many times it is delivered.

    Handler writes and the processed marker commit atomically. Failures are recorded on the inbox row and re-raised for broker retry or dead-lettering.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    event Mapping[str, Any]

    The received message. id_key/type_key name its id and type members (id/type, as in CloudEvents, by default).

    		 required
    registry HandlerRegistry

    Type → handler.

    		 required
    inbox_model type[AbstractInboxMessage]

    The consuming app's concrete inbox model.

    		 required
    clock Callable[[], datetime]

    Supplies received_at/processed_at.

    		 now

    Returns:

    Type Description
    bool

    True when the handler ran, False for a duplicate delivery.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    UnknownMessageType

    No handler is registered for the type.
